title: Multi-file upload queues one BullMQ job per file and flips overall status to completed only when every file finishes
description: Grounded in evidence-upload.controller.js queueUploadJobs() and evidence-upload.worker.js updateOverallStatus(): each file gets its own 'process-upload' job (3 attempts, exponential backoff from 5s), and the worker recomputes evidence.uploadStatus.status after every job settles, only flipping to 'completed' once processed === total files.
preconditions: BullMQ 'file-upload' queue and worker running against a test Redis instance
steps: POST /evidence/upload with 3 files attached to one evidence item
Poll GET /evidence/:evidenceId/upload-status until all files report a terminal state
Inspect each file's files[].s3.key, files[].checksum.value, and the overall uploadStatus.status
expectedResult: Three separate BullMQ jobs are created. Each file transitions pending → uploading → completed with an SHA-256 checksum and S3 key populated. uploadStatus.status only becomes 'completed' after the 3rd file finishes, not after the 1st or 2nd.

title: Editing evidence title/description bumps the version but does not carry forward control mappings by default
description: createVersionedUpdate() in evidence-version.service.js only clones active EvidenceControlMappings to the new version when opts.carryForwardMappings === true. evidence.controller.js updateEvidence passes `req.body.carryForwardMappings === true`, so an ordinary PUT with no explicit flag defaults to false and the mapped controls stay pinned to the old version.
preconditions: Evidence item at v1 has 2 active control mappings
No carryForwardMappings field sent in the update body
steps: PUT /evidence/:evidenceId with a changed title (a version-trigger field) and no carryForwardMappings key
GET /evidence/mappings?evidenceId=<id> filtered to the new version
expectedResult: Evidence is now at v2. The 2 control mappings created against v1 are NOT present when querying mappings for v2 — control coverage for this evidence appears to drop until mappings are manually recreated or the caller explicitly passes carryForwardMappings:true.

title: Restoring a historical version defaults to carrying forward the current version's active control mappings
description: EvidenceVersionService.restoreVersion() sets carryForwardMappings = (opts.carryForwardMappings !== false) — the opposite default from a normal edit (EVID-INT-002). This asymmetry is intentional per the code comment (dropping mappings on restore previously zeroed out coverage with no warning) but the two endpoints behaving oppositely by default is a real trap for anyone assuming consistent behavior.
preconditions: Evidence item has 2 versions; v2 (current) has 1 active control mapping
steps: POST /evidence/:evidenceId/versions/1/restore with an empty body (no carryForwardMappings key)
GET /evidence/mappings?evidenceId=<id> filtered to the newly created version (v3)
expectedResult: v3 is created from v1's content. The mapping that was active on v2 is cloned onto v3 automatically, with no explicit flag required — confirming restore's carry-forward default is true, opposite of updateEvidence's default.

title: Archiving evidence cascades to deactivate its linked vulnerability/patch-management/SBOM report records
description: deactivateLinkedReports() in evidence.controller.js runs on archiveEvidence, transitionWorkflow(→'archived'), and hardDeleteEvidence. It sets isActive:false on PatchManagementReport/PatchItem/VulnReport/VulnFinding/SbomReport/SbomComponent documents linked by evidenceId, so those modules' active lists and aggregate stats stop counting the archived source evidence.
preconditions: A vulnerability_report evidence item exists with a parsed VulnReport (isActive: true) and at least one VulnFinding
steps: DELETE /evidence/:evidenceId (archive) on the vulnerability_report evidence item
Query the vulnerability-report module's active list/aggregate endpoint for the same project
expectedResult: The archived evidence's VulnReport and all its VulnFinding documents are updated to isActive:false and no longer appear in the vulnerability-report module's active counts, without requiring a separate manual action in that module.

title: Exceeding the org's storage quota flags the evidence as overLimit but does not block the upload
description: createEvidence() calls quota.consume(orgId, 'storageBytes', totalBytes). On QUOTA_EXCEEDED it sets storageOverLimit = true and continues — the evidence document still gets created with overLimit:true and the files are still queued for S3 upload. This is a soft cap by design, not a hard block.
preconditions: isPricingV1Enabled is true for the test org
The org's storage quota is already at or near its limit
steps: POST /evidence/upload with a file whose size pushes the org over its storageBytes quota
expectedResult: The request returns 201, not 402/403. The created evidence has overLimit:true and its files still proceed through the normal BullMQ → S3 pipeline — the org is not prevented from uploading further evidence purely by quota.

title: AI-assisted upload creates the evidence draft even when the AI extraction call fails
description: uploadAI() runs queueUploadJobs() (S3) and callAIService() (notebookAI-service) concurrently via Promise.allSettled — neither result blocks the other, and AI failure is captured into aiAssistedUpload.aiSuggestions.error rather than thrown.
preconditions: NOTEBOOK_AI_SERVICE_URL points to a service that will return a 500/timeout for this test
steps: POST /evidence/upload/ai with a valid file while the AI extraction service is unreachable
expectedResult: Response is 201 with the evidence in 'draft' status. aiAssistedUpload.processingStatus is 'failed', aiAssistedUpload.aiSuggestions.error is true with a message, and the file's S3 upload still proceeds independently through the normal BullMQ pipeline.

title: Fulfilling an evidence request accepts a draft evidence item with zero attached files
description: linkEvidence() in evidence-request.controller.js resolves evidenceId to a Mongo _id and immediately sets status:'fulfilled' — it never checks the linked Evidence document's status (draft/rejected/expired all pass) or whether evidence.files has any entries. A request can be marked fulfilled by evidence that is not actually reviewable.
preconditions: An Evidence item exists in 'draft' status with an empty files[] array
steps: POST /evidence-requests/:requestId/link with evidenceId pointing at the draft, file-less evidence item
expectedResult: Current behavior: the request transitions to 'fulfilled' with fulfilledAt set and linkedEvidenceId populated — no validation error is raised despite the linked evidence having no files and never having been submitted for review.

title: resolveProjectScope narrows the evidence list to the caller's assigned projects when no projectId is supplied
description: PLAC-006: listEvidence() calls Object.assign(filter, await resolveProjectScope(req, projectId)). Omitting projectId must restrict results to projects the caller is a member of, not fall back to every project in the org.
preconditions: Org has Project A and Project B, each with evidence
Test user is a member of Project A only
steps: As the test user, call GET /evidence with no projectId query param
expectedResult: Only Project A's evidence is returned. Project B's evidence (same org, different project, no membership) is excluded — the response is not org-wide.
